What Should You Do If You Have a Flat Tyre?

If you notice a puncture or sudden loss of tyre pressure while driving, the first priority is getting yourself and other passengers somewhere safe.

If it is safe to do so:

  • Slow down gradually
  • Avoid sudden steering or braking
  • Move to a safe location away from moving traffic
  • Switch on your hazard lights
  • Keep passengers away from the road
  • Do not continue driving on a severely damaged tyre
  • Contact roadside assistance if the vehicle cannot safely continue

If you are stopped in a dangerous position or there is an immediate risk to people, contact the emergency services first.

GOOD TO KNOW

Common Causes of a Flat Tyre

A flat tyre can happen for different reasons. Some common causes include:

Puncture

A nail, screw, glass or another sharp object can penetrate the tyre and cause air to escape.

Damaged Sidewall

Impact with a kerb, pothole or another object can damage the tyre sidewall.

Loss of Air Pressure

A tyre may gradually lose pressure because of a slow puncture, valve issue or other problem.

Pothole Damage

A significant pothole can damage a tyre or wheel and may result in a sudden loss of pressure.

Worn Tyre

A heavily worn tyre may be more vulnerable to damage and may no longer provide safe road contact.

Valve Problem

A damaged or faulty valve can also contribute to loss of tyre pressure.

The exact cause is not always obvious from the roadside, so avoid assuming that simply adding air has solved the problem if the tyre continues to lose pressure.

Puncture Assistance Birmingham

A puncture does not always mean the same thing.

Some punctures may be repairable, while other tyre damage may make the tyre unsuitable for further use. Sidewall damage, severe impact damage or a badly damaged tyre may require a replacement tyre or vehicle recovery rather than a simple repair.

For this reason, do not continue driving simply because the vehicle still appears to move.

If you are unsure about the condition of your tyre, stop in a safe location and seek appropriate assistance.

Tyre Damage After a Pothole or Kerb Impact

Not every tyre problem is caused by a puncture.

A pothole or kerb impact can potentially cause damage to:

  • The tyre tread
  • Tyre sidewall
  • Wheel rim
  • Wheel alignment
  • Suspension components

If you have hit a pothole or kerb and the vehicle subsequently feels different, pulls to one side or develops a flat tyre, it may be safer to stop and have the vehicle checked rather than continuing your journey.

If the vehicle cannot safely move, recovery may be required.

KEY SITUATIONS

Flat Tyre vs Slow Puncture

A sudden flat tyre is easy to notice, but some punctures develop gradually.

Sudden Flat

The tyre loses a significant amount of pressure quickly, potentially leaving the vehicle difficult or unsafe to drive.

Slow Puncture

The tyre loses air gradually. You may notice that the same tyre needs regular inflation or that the tyre-pressure warning light keeps appearing. A slow puncture should not simply be ignored. Repeated pressure loss can indicate a tyre or valve problem that needs attention.

If the tyre becomes too low to drive safely, arrange roadside assistance rather than continuing on it.

Tyre Pressure Warning Light

Modern vehicles may display a tyre-pressure warning when one or more tyres have lost pressure.

If the warning appears:

  • Check the tyre pressures when it is safe to do so
  • Look for visible tyre damage
  • Avoid driving on a visibly flat tyre
  • Follow the vehicle manufacturer’s guidance
  • Seek assistance if you are unsure whether the tyre is safe

A warning light does not necessarily mean the tyre is punctured, but it should not be ignored.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can you help with a flat tyre in Birmingham?

Yes. A.A.D Transport & Recovery provides roadside recovery support for drivers dealing with flat tyres and tyre-related vehicle problems across Birmingham and surrounding areas.

Do you provide 24/7 flat tyre assistance?

Yes. A.A.D Transport & Recovery provides 24/7 recovery support. Contact the team with your location and explain the tyre problem.

What should I do if I get a puncture while driving?

Slow down carefully, avoid sudden steering or braking, and move to a safe location if possible. Do not continue driving on a severely damaged or flat tyre. If you cannot safely deal with the problem, contact roadside assistance.

Can I drive on a completely flat tyre?

It is generally not advisable to drive on a completely flat tyre. Doing so can cause further tyre or wheel damage and may affect vehicle handling. Stop safely and arrange appropriate assistance.

What if I do not have a spare tyre?

If your vehicle has no usable spare tyre, you may need roadside assistance or recovery. Provide your vehicle details, location, and tyre condition when contacting A.A.D Transport & Recovery.

Can you help with a slow puncture?

A slow puncture should not be ignored. If the tyre continues losing pressure or becomes unsafe to drive, contact roadside assistance to discuss the appropriate next step.

What if my tyre was damaged by a pothole?

A pothole can damage a tyre, wheel or other vehicle components. If your tyre has lost pressure or you notice unusual handling after hitting a pothole, stop safely and seek appropriate assistance.

Can a flat tyre damage the wheel?

Yes. Continuing to drive on a severely deflated tyre can potentially cause additional damage to the wheel. If you cannot maintain safe tyre pressure, avoid unnecessary driving and arrange assistance.

Can you recover a car if the tyre cannot be repaired?

If the tyre cannot be safely repaired or replaced at the roadside and the vehicle cannot continue, vehicle recovery may be required. A.A.D Transport & Recovery can discuss the recovery options based on the vehicle and location.

What information should I provide when requesting flat tyre assistance?

Provide your exact location, vehicle make and model, affected tyre, description of the problem, whether the tyre is completely flat and whether you have a usable spare.

What areas do you cover?

A.A.D Transport & Recovery provides recovery services across Birmingham and surrounding areas. If you are unsure whether your exact location is covered, provide your location when contacting the team to confirm availability.

Modern vehicles may display a tyre-pressure warning when one or more tyres have lost pressure.

If the warning appears:

  • Check the tyre pressures when it is safe to do so
  • Look for visible tyre damage
  • Avoid driving on a visibly flat tyre
  • Follow the vehicle manufacturer's guidance
  • Seek assistance if you are unsure whether the tyre is safe

A warning light does not necessarily mean the tyre is punctured, but it should not be ignored.
